name: 3D GITHUB VISUALIZER
oneLiner: Any GitHub profile as a navigable 3D universe, in three draw calls a frame

headline.claim: It built cleanly and rendered a blank white page — because headless Chromium has no WebGL, so every automated check had been screenshotting an empty canvas and passing.

honest: Deployment routing is untested: the bug that took the live proxy down for every real path was invisible to all 74 tests, because they exercise a handler production never invoked. Frame-time figures come from a single Apple M4 Pro; there is no measurement on integrated graphics, which is what MOTION.md actually asked for. On Fast 3G the first frame lands at 2665 ms, missing the project's own 2 s bar, and the unsplit build misses it too. Commit history is still authored by a bot. Three language aliases are inert, so F#, Objective-C and Shell render grey.

built.audit: Built clean at exit 0 with no console errors and rendered a near-blank white page: the canvas mounted position:fixed with no z-index and painted over the header, an alpha renderer let a light-theme background show through, and eleven components each positioned themselves independently.
repaired: Canvas painted over the header — a missing z-index, not a missing component
Sphere radius was applied twice, so rendered radius was size squared and small repositories vanished
A WebGL failure set an error state that nothing ever rendered, so a visitor without WebGL got a silent empty page
Headless Chromium has no WebGL, so every automated check had been passing against an empty canvas
The browser suite hardcoded a port and started no server, and once ran end-to-end against a different application
C++ and C# fell through to the grey Other bucket because "C++".toLowerCase() is not the map key
Blue and indigo survived the design-system purge inside rgba(), invisible to a hex-only guard
The favicon had never resolved — index.html referenced a scaffold file the repo never contained
Deleted 37 process documents, including ten test reports written against zero tests
measured: Splitting Three.js out of the entry chunk cost 944 ms to first frame on Fast 3G until a build-time modulepreload was added — the obvious optimisation was a regression until it was measured
Frame interval is useless on fast hardware: 100 and 250 repositories both reported 4.2 ms, which is the display refresh, so the harness records time inside the render loop instead
Rank-mapped axes replaced a linear min-max, because stars and forks are power-law distributed and a linear map collapsed the universe into one mass

decisions.what: An allowlist proxy, not a passthrough
decisions.why: Four endpoint patterns are proxied and everything else 403s. Without it, /api/github/<anything> would be an open proxy authenticating with our token, including /user, which would reveal whose token it is.

decisions.what: Guard the blocking payload instead of silencing Vite's chunk warning
decisions.why: Tree-shaken three is 545.56 kB against 750.94 kB for its own full minified build; the remainder is WebGLRenderer. Raising chunkSizeWarningLimit would mute a real regression detector, so a guard asserts the entry chunk plus its static imports stays under 500 kB with three absent.

decisions.what: The empty state is the product
decisions.why: Most visitors never type a username. A seeded 88-node galaxy renders with no API call, so the first ten seconds are never blank and can never rate-limit.

decisions.what: Scene-graph layout is optional but all-or-nothing
decisions.why: A producer without coordinates should not have to invent them, but half a layout would place some nodes meaningfully and the rest at the origin, which reads as a bug rather than as data.

github.description: Any GitHub profile rendered as a navigable 3D universe. React, Three.js, WebGL — one instanced draw call per frame and a designed empty state.
